title: Sims Competitor InZoi Deletes “Uncomfortable” Post After Fan Pushback
description: The ambitious life-simulation game InZoi was once heralded as a potential "Sims-killer"--a promising new title that fans of the genre could turn to following EA's relentless pursuit to monetize every aspect of The Sims 4. However, a lackluster early-access period and concerns over the game's liberal use of AI made for a rocky start. Over the past year and a half, developer Krafton has addressed some of the complaints leveled at the game, but now, it finds itself in hot water for a different reason. Earlier today, the official InZoi X account shared a post depicting a balding man in a leather coat watching children play on a playground alongside the caption, "Just a peaceful day at the playground. Nothing unusual here... just ignore the bald guy" alongside an eyes emoji. Though the post is still up on the game's official Discord server, it was removed on X a few hours after it was initially posted due to users calling the post disturbing and pointing out that it seemed to allude to pedophilia. After removing the post, the account issued the following statement: The account initially shared the post to showcase improvements being made to InZoi's playgrounds as well as promote the game's upcoming Celebrity DLC, which is slated to arrive this December. However, its easy to understand why fans had a negative reaction to the post--especially in light of recent events. InZoi isn't the only life simulation game in the news for less-than-ideal reasons. After a brutal round of layoffs and announcing the closure of Mass Effect and Dragon Age studio BioWare, EA revealed that one of Maxis' ongoing Sims projects is being paused.

title: Fangs For The Memories: The Best Vampires In Video Games
description: For many of us, the weather is finally becoming that cool autumn crisp, the days are getting shorter, and the season for gorging on candy and horror movies is in full-swing. While I may be in the camp that believes there aren’t nearly enough vampire video games, these creatures of the night are well represented in games. So what better time to pay tribute to our favorite bloodsuckers? Show off those pearly white fangs; these are the best vampires in gaming: Astarion - Baldur’s Gate III One of the best companions of the generational RPG by Larian Studios, Astarion’s charm will win over even the coldest of hearts. Players who choose to engage with his storyline are treated to some of the best storytelling Baldur’s Gate III has to offer. Did I mention he’s a rogue class by default, too? It was incredibly fun speccing his build to stealthily one-shot enemies and retain plenty of action points for his vampiric abilities. Rayne - BloodRayne A protagonist of a bygone era, Rayne was the definition of both sexy and deadly. Featuring an outfit that would fit right in an Underworld film, Rayne uses nimble acrobatics to slay and feast on unsuspecting foes such as Nazis and pesky cult members. While she hasn’t had a title since 2011’s BloodRayne: Betrayal, I pray to the vampiric gods that one day Rayne will return. Blade - Marvel's Midnight Suns This one feels like cheating. We all know how badass Blade is from the 1998 film, but his portrayal in Midnight Suns particularly stands out among vampires in games, adding a whole new side of humanity to the notorious vampire slayer. As the player, you have access to all of Blade’s vampiric abilities, which make short work of foes, but you also have the ability to get to know him personally (including his secret crush on Captain Marvel). Vincent Valentine - Final Fantasy VII Have you ever just seen a character that is the embodiment of cool? That sums up Vincent Valentine in a nutshell. Hell, when Cloud and company first encounter him,…

title: Leave It To Double Fine To Make The First Single-Player Friendslop Game
description: Friendslop is everywhere these days. Take one glance at the most recent Steam Next Fest and you’ll be inundated with not only mountains of obnoxious AI slop, but countless games where you and a group of friends can get up to wacky hijinks with cartoonish avatars, over the top physics, and hilarious use of proximity chat. If you’re a developer and your take on this genre goes viral, it has a chance of attracting tens of thousands of players and being a massive financial success--it’s no surprise that friendslop has become so commonplace. But if you fancy gaming on your lonesome for once or sadly don’t have any friends but still want to embrace the chaos of friendslop, then the latest game by Double Fine could be right up your street. Just make sure a bus filled with rowdy passengers doesn’t run you down as you start walking down it. Thank You Bus Driver is available on Steam for only $5 and it’s a delightfully wacky adventure that does exactly what it says on the tin. You are a bus driver working in a small monochrome city and must drive passengers to their destination. Do so by completing certain objectives like stopping people from eating smelly food or dozing off and you’ll earn a "Thank You" for your troubles. I don’t think falling asleep on the bus is that much of a bad thing (though I suppose it might get you mugged in London). Your task isn’t just about driving from place to place though, you also need to keep your passengers in line by turning around and smacking them with your freakishly long arms. And if someone refuses to stop, you can easily throw them out the backdoor into oncoming traffic. Lovely stuff. Well, it would be if you didn’t also need to keep driving at the exact same time and reach your next destination before the shift timer runs out. Double Fine has crafted a gameplay formula that is easy to understand yet deceptively hard to master while giving off the very same lunacy I’ve experienced in games like Peak or REPO. And that's just…

title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s First DLC Is Out Now, Honors A Real Soldier Who Sustained Gruesome Injuries
description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 released today, October 23, and the game's first DLC pack is available now. In keeping with Call of Duty tradition, the day-one DLC is a Call of Duty Endowment (CODE) pack, with proceeds going to Activision's charity that supports military veterans find new jobs after they leave the service. The CODE Valor Pack adds the real-life Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter to the game as a playable character. Carpenter was in Marjah, Afghanistan, when, on November 21, 2010, he put himself in front of a grenade to help save the life of his fellow Marine, Nick Eufrazio. Carpenter sustained serious injuries from the grenade blast. He was unconscious for five weeks, had his teeth stripped from his mouth, and lost an eye. He sustained numerous other life-threatening injuries in the blast. Carpenter received the Medal of Honor from President Barack Obama in 2014. At the ceremony, Obama said, "They found Kyle lying face down, directly over the blast area. His helmet was riddled with holes. His gear was melted. Part of his Kevlar vest was blown away. One of the doctors who treated him later said Kyle was, 'Literally wounded from the top of his head to his feet.'" Carpenter underwent brain surgery to remove shrapnel from his head. He had about 40 other surgeries to addresses his injuries, which included a collapsed lung, fractured fingers, and one arm that broke in more than 30 places. He had multiple skin grafts and now has a prosthetic eye, a new jaw, and new teeth. The Valor Pack includes the Relentless and Valor skins, along with new weapon blueprints, a combat knife, and a weapon charm, among other things. All proceeds from the $20 DLC bundles will go to the CODE charity. Everything in the new MW4 CODE DLC. title: Shepard Actor Reacts To Leaked Mass Effect Trailer, Is “Holding Hope” The Game Will Live On
description: Prolific and veteran gaming actor Jennifer Hale, who is known for voicing Commander Shepard in the Mass Effect series, has reacted to the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of the next game in the series. After footage of the new project, Mass Effect Universe, was released, Hale said, "It's extraordinary." She added: "I’m holding hope for magic to happen. This community and you incredible vevs deserve that and more." A "Save Mass Effect" Change.org petition was launched this week to urge EA to "take decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect." The petition has more than 65,000 signatures so far. All of BioWare's new releases in the past decade--Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard--were commercial disappointments. Against that backdrop, closing the studio makes a lot of financial sense, but it's upsetting to the millions of Mass Effect fans who adore the franchise and want to see it continue. Based on insider reporting, the new Mass Effect game would have mixed covert ops with John Wick-inspired action, and that got a lot of people excited about what could have been. Composer Bear McCreary, who has done work for the God of War and Call of Duty franchises, reacted to BioWare's closure, too. Asked if the laid-off BioWare developers could take what they had and complete the project as a "spiritual successor" via crowdfunding, McCreary said it's a good idea but is probably unrealistic. "Man, I want to believe. But, I just gotta ask... How many examples are there of this really working in the past? And of those examples, how many were a project as big as Mass Effect?" he said. Avi Lewis, a Canadian politician, has called on the government to help save BioWare by providing “federal support” to the workers to buy it back. “This is private equity, this is what it does,” he said. “Buy up businesses, run them into the ground, and rip them apart for short-term profit. The developers at BioWare know how to run the…

title: The Next Mass Effect Sounded Like John Wick In Space
description: After news broke that EA would be shutting down BioWare, more details on the studio's in-development Mass Effect have begun to trickle out. A trailer for Mass Effect Universe hinted that the next game in the series would have a completely different tone, moving away from the galactic warfare that defined the first three games and toward covert ops, espionage, and the occasional barroom shootout. Gaming content creator and YouTuber Dantics has shed more light on the game, describing it as a Mass Effect game for the fans. Known for his lore videos, including several on Mass Effect, Dantics says he was part of a private "Mass Effect Council," a community feedback group of content creators who helped advise BioWare's small team. Dantics says that Mass Effect Universe was set over 600 years after the Reaper War, and players would step into the boots of a customizable N7 agent. Players would also have a much smaller arsenal of weapons that would make them feel like a "cross between John Wick and James Bond," and they'd be working to take down a sinister force that was operating in the shadows of a galactic cold war. While Commander Shepard was a soldier, your N7 character was going to be an "agent" who would rely on cunning to get through encounters, but could apply pressure when needed--ballistic pressure, that is. Following the destruction of the relays at the end of the Reaper War, the fast-travel hubs had been rebuilt, and technology had advanced at a rapid pace. Shepard's legacy had been preserved centuries after their death; three new powerful alliances had arisen: Council races had formed their own faction, while humanity had aligned itself with Krogans, Batarians, and other superpowers. The Geth--a synthetic, network-based artificial intelligence species--had become a third power, and Dantics said there would be connections between the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies, thanks to the Geth building superstructure relays. So what would the gameplay have been like?…

title: Dead By Daylight Delistings Continue As Developer Reveals It Must F**k With The Chuck
description: Dead by Daylight features dozens of characters, including many licensed heroes and villains from beloved horror franchises, but every once in a while, some of them get delisted. Behaviour Interactive has revealed that Chucky will soon suffer such a fate; he's being delisted on November 24 at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET. Until then, players can grab him and any related cosmetics on sale. Chucky, whose in-game nickname is The Good Guy, debuted in Dead by Daylight in November 2023. Like all characters, he came with three unique perks, all of which will stay in the game after he's gone, Behaviour said. Anyone who has purchased Chucky will retain access to him, as well as any of his alternate skins, like the Tiffany alternate skin voiced by Jennifer Tilly and based on Chucky's wife, Tiffany. For players who own the Chucky DLC, his perks will keep their established names, while anyone who doesn't unlock the DLC before it disappears from all platforms will see his perks change names. You can read those name changes below: Hex: Two Can Play will be called Hex: Eye For An Eye Friends Til the End will be called One Track Mind Batteries Included will be called Gaining Steam Other rewards tied to Chucky, like Prestige rewards and possible quests that allow players to use him, will remain available. "Hi, I'm Chucky. Wanna play? You have one month to unlock access." Behaviour didn't say exactly why Chucky is being delisted. We can assume the rights are expiring, but whether that's simply based on the terms of the original deal or if something changed later on is unknown. For DBD long-timers, this sadly isn't the first time players have had to say goodbye to a famous face who once appeared in the game. Last December, it was revealed that Michael Myers and his related map would be removed from the game. Since the map was part of a free update, it's been removed for the entire community. Earlier in 2025, Pinhead from Hellraiser was also delisted. Like Chucky, players who purchased Myers or…

title: Best Loadouts In Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Multiplayer
description: Modern Warfare 4 has fully released, and there are plenty of new guns and attachments to unlock for this new year of Call of Duty. In this guide, we'll suggest some recommended weapon builds, so you can see exactly which guns and attachments you'll want to focus on unlocking and leveling up early. Call of Duty's Gunsmith feature returns in Modern Warfare 4. This customization system lets you create five-attachment builds for multiplayer. In addition to the standard five attachments, you can also include the gun's unique Apex attachment. Apex attachments are special add-ons you can unlock for each gun, which will drastically change how the weapon is used. Apex attachments are similar to the weapon conversion kits found in the recent Call of Duty games, but in Modern Warfare 4 they don't cost one of your attachment slots. Apex attachments aren’t unlocked until you’ve reached the maximum weapon level for a specific gun. Some of these attachments are a bit wacky and aren't practical add-ons, but others will offer viable bonuses to your weapon. All of our recommended multiplayer builds for Modern Warfare 4 can be viewed below. HAN 86 HAN 86 assault rifle The HAN 86 assault rifle is one of the best choices for mid-to long-range combat, and this gun is fairly easy to use in multiplayer. The recommended attachments will boost the damage range, improve bullet velocity, and quicken your aim-down-sight speed. title: CoD: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ – Best Hot Spots And Loot Locations
description: Modern Warfare 4 is live with Call of Duty's new DMZ extraction mode, where scavenging guns, equipment, and resources is crucial to survival. All main POIs on Hajin Hajin has 13 main points-of-interest, but some POIs are going to offer more valuable looting opportunities, depending on what items you're hoping to scavenge. There is one area in particular that can offer several containers of high-end items, and we'll give you a route that will cause the least amount of resistance from enemy forces. You can access this area at any time in your match, but we recommend choosing the story mission called Operation Iron Citadel. This saves time by spawning you very close to the POI at the start of your match, and you'll have an objective marker that leads you to the exact loot room you'll be looking for. Follow along the outer wall of the air base, and eventually you'll see a broken wall you can vault over. Stealth is recommended here, using suppressed weapons or throwing knives to take down any guards you might encounter. However, you shouldn't run into many guards with this route, assuming you stay quiet and don't alert the whole base. title: WoW: Forever’s Divisive Layering Will See Major Improvements For Launch, Blizzard Says
description: World of Warcraft: Forever's layering system will receive some significant improvements for launch, according to a statement provided to GameSpot from Blizzard. Layering, for the uninitiated, is a behind-the-scenes system in WoW: Forever that essentially creates and runs new versions (or layers) of the world as needed, all running simultaneously on top of one another. According to Blizzard, players in WoW: Forever are assigned a layer based on various criteria, like familiar players and friends, language, and PvP balance. Grouping up with a player or friend who is on another layer will transport you to the same layer so you can interact. There are some pros to this system. It makes completing quests easier (since there's less competition for quests items and enemies) and the world far less crowded. It also helps performance, as anytime there are thousands of players in a concentrated area, like a capital city, the game can struggle to handle the load. Layering spreads those players out. It works wonders in modern WoW and has also been used to different degrees in various versions of WoW Classic in the past. Unfortunately, there are also some huge downsides that have repeatedly surfaced over the course of the WoW: Forever beta. It doesn't take much searching on YouTube or Reddit to find countless instances of players complaining about layering. Leaving a group, crossing into a different zone, or traveling on a zeppelin or boat causes players to abruptly switch layers. The layering changes feel far more frequent and noticeable than in the past, ruining some of the charm that comes from having a persistent world filled with the same people. Thankfully, changes are on the way. title: Your Mind Is Playing Tricks On You: Why You Hear What You Want To Hear In Control Resonant
description: Control Resonant is delightfully weird: a sequel that isn't afraid to fly its freak flag as it pits you against all manner of supernatural phenomena wreaking havoc on Manhattan. But between bosses that resemble Francis Bacon-inspired nightmare fuel and other spooky occurrences, The Board is undoubtedly the scene-stealer of Control Resonant--and that's without you even seeing them! The Board is louder than ever as it accompanies Dylan Faden in Remedy's new game, seemingly trapped in the powerful shape-shifting artifact that he uses to smash his way through The Hiss and The Patterning. A successful run elicits booming words of encouragement/motivation/incentive from the paranatural entities that make up The Board, each interaction being the equivalent of a shotgun blast of indecipherable bass that'll tickle your audio receptors. So what goes into designing and developing a "character" like The Board? A surprising amount of technical wizardry and experimentation, as Lucas Pierrot, audio lead on Control Resonant, explained. The Board is right here, and you get to experience the full council Compared to Control, The Board's audio identity is very different. Gone are the sounds of telephonic voices, replaced with something more uniquely alien and commanding. Why the change? As Pierrot explained, The Board spoke to players through a hotline in Control, but in Control Resonant, they have a direct line of communication to Dylan, and by extension, the player. "From an audio perspective, the main shift is now [that] The Board is speaking directly into Dylan’s mind, in full definition," Pierrot said. "In the original Control, the board talks through the hotline, an old phone connecting you to a remote mysterious place, hence the static and muffled audio. Here there are no filters anymore. The Board is right here, and you get to experience the full council." A symbolic version of anger The Board was the first audio concept made for Control Resonant, with work on the entity…

title: In A (Biddy) Blas Of Glory: How Star Wars: Galactic Racer’s Smallest Racer Made Such A Huge Impact
description: Biddy Blas could probably use a booster cushion on his speeder to see more clearly over its handlebars, but he hasn't needed any sort of booster to make a massive impression on the internet. This squat, reptilian nuisance from Star Wars: Galactic Racer has overtaken social media algorithms with a ceaseless flood of fan-made skits, memes, and thirst traps. Blas and his shrill Huttese barks have acted almost as unexpected marketing for the game, seemingly having a greater reach and impact than the smattering of high review scores. And like a podracer barreling down the Mos Espa Raceway, it has all come at Richard Summers-Calvert, the voice behind the Crocin racer, incredibly quickly. "I knew we had created something special," Summers-Calvert told GameSpot. "I knew we created something people would really enjoy and [Blas] was going to be really irritating. And I remember posting on my Instagram Stories [something vague] like, ‘I just had a really lovely session. Can’t wait for you all to see it.’ And that post popped up again recently, and I really did feel great that day going home. And I was like, ‘We’ve definitely done something cool.’ I had no idea it would be this successful and this positive." Similarly struck by this success is Galactic Racer's music and narrative director, Nathaniel Daw, who was quick to recall the initial, eye-opening recording sessions with Summers-Calvert. According to Daw, the Star Wars-free early scripts--which were filled with all sorts of codenames meant to obfuscate what title voice actors were actually reading for--didn’t give Summers-Calvert much to go on other than this mystery character having a tiny stature that betrayed his large ego. And despite the opaqueness, the muscular, red-headed actor took a bold swing. "About halfway through, he just lets out this incredible laugh," recalled Daw in an interview with GameSpot. "And that’s basically Biddy’s [current] laugh. And at that point, we sort of knew. It had the energy that is so…

title: Arkane Lyon Could Be Shut Down Within Weeks As Deadline To Find A Buyer Looms
description: It might be the end of the road for Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Lyon, as a new report says that the studio has until November 13 to find a buyer or face closure. Le Monde reported that while Microsoft had followed the procedure as laid out in Florange Law--French legislation that requires Microsoft to spend at least three months searching for a buyer for Arkane Lyon--negotiations were going "badly," and worker unions are currently attempting to buy more time to save jobs at the studio, which is currently still working on Marvel's Blade. The report says "several forms of takeover" are being considered, but the union's plans could include re-employing affected staff at other Xbox studios or taking Microsoft to court. According to IGN, development on Marvel's Blade was still on track for a new reveal in early 2027, followed by a Q4 2027 release. The game was originally revealed in December 2023, but aside from a handful of concept art images since then, nothing else has been shown. Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier also corroborated reports of "multiple paths" being explored and that he'd be surprised if the studio is shut down. If Arkane Lyon is facing closure, it'll be the end of a studio that has been around for 27 years. Its first game was Arx Fatalis in 2002, and it followed that up with the release of Dark Messiah of Might and Magic (2006) and KarmaStar (2009). Since the 2010s, the studio has pumped out several hits like the Dishonored games and Deathloop. The Texas-based studio that it operated, Arkane Austin, was established in 2006, but following the release of the critically panned Redfall in 2023, it was shut down in 2024. Arkane Lyon's departure from the Xbox Games Studio portfolio was announced earlier this year, alongside Double Fine Productions, Compulsion Games, Undead Labs, and Ninja Theory. title: Woim is the earth-guzzling, self-bisecting sokoban pick-me-up I needed after a week of games industry disasters
description: While ladling city-builders into the Maw's feeding trough this week, I remarked that being a worm must really suck. Then came the closure of BioWare, layoffs across other EA studios, further depressing genAI revelations, allegations of antisemitism at indie gaming events, a big Capcom data breach, and yet more worrying tidyings about Arkane. I rescind my earlier observation: I would like to be a worm. A happy little worm, tunnelling after golden apples in the moist and forgiving earth, where there are no emails or press releases at all. The only thing I have to worry about down here is my butt growing so big I get stuck behind it. And also getting chopped in half by sliding doors, but it turns out this may actually help with the first problem. See for yourself - video below. Read more
